title: Scheduler granularity & mixlen prefetch throttling for continuous batcher
creator: Priya Kapoor
description: We observe tail latency spikes and increased GPU memory churn for mixed prompt/response workloads. Short prompts with long generated responses (and vice versa) cause inefficient slot packing and premature KV eviction. This ticket tunes the continuous batching scheduler to add fine-grained admission windows, adaptive prefetch throttles, and a small hysteresis layer to stabilize KV residency and reduce GPU slab fragmentation.
background: Recent incidents (see ENG-472888, ENG-314159) surfaced cases where bursty short prompts caused KV churn that evicted warm prefixes needed for long-turn generations, increasing token compute and latency. Existing schedulers use global admission and coarse time-slicing which is suboptimal for workloads with bimodal length distributions (chat apps, code assistants). Previous experiments focused on coarse length buckets; this work targets scheduler granularity, prefetch pacing, and a KV-hysteresis policy to reduce thrashing while preserving throughput and SLOs.
proposal_summary: Introduce a scheduler-granularity feature that: (1) maintains per-cohort micro-windows (5-30ms) for admission based on recent length histograms; (2) implements an adaptive prefetch throttle that limits speculative KV prefetches when free GPU slab < threshold; (3) a 2-stage KV hysteresis that delays eviction of recently-used prefixes for short windows to favor long-turn completion. Rollout via feature flag and A/B on dedicated pool. Tune thresholds with closed-loop metrics.
acceptance_criteria: P95 latency for mixed-bimodal workload improves by >= 12% compared to baseline (same throughput)
KV eviction rate per-minute decreases by >= 25% on test harness with synthetic mixlen traces
GPU memory fragmentation (measured by free-slab variance) reduces by >= 15%
Does not reduce aggregate throughput by more than 5% on standard benchmarks
Feature rollout gated behind e2e tests, perf dashboards, and sign-off from runtime PM
implementation_plan: Spike (2 days): implement per-cohort micro-window admission; run small-scale replay against 3 mixlen traces
Experiment (5 days): add adaptive prefetch throttle based on 'free_slab_bytes' signal; instrument counters and early stop path
KV policy (3 days): implement 2-stage hysteresis with window decay tuned by sequence length and recency
Integration (2 days): feature-flag, rollout orchestration, canary config for dedicated pool
Validation (3 days): run long-run 72h soak with production-like traffic, collect dashboards and snapshots
Rollout (1 day): progressive ramp to 100% on non-critical clusters, monitor, then schedule across remaining capacity
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Overly aggressive prefetch throttle could harm tail throughput — Mitigation: conservative defaults, metric-driven adaptive scaling
Risk: Hysteresis may cause KV pollution if windows are too long — Mitigation: add decay and per-prefix heat counters, experiment with 50/150/500ms windows
Risk: Complexity increases scheduler CPU overhead — Mitigation: microbenchmark CPU usage and fall back to coarse mode if CPU > threshold
Risk: Interaction with autoscaling policies — Mitigation: test with Dedicated autoscale configs and coordinate with infra team
metrics_and_dashboards: mixlen-p95-latency: per-pool and per-model P95/P99 for synthetic mixlen traces
kv-evictions-per-minute: broken down by prefix-length and cohort
gpu-free-slab-variance: slab fragmentation metric across GPUs in pool
